conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; sides field states mirrored/same

candidates.name: TwentyGapBarSetup
candidates.quote: When the market stays on one side of the moving average without touching it for 20 consecutive bars or more, the trend is strong, but it is also overdone and will likely soon pull back to the moving average.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a persistent counter of consecutive bars whose high-low range has not touched the N-bar EMA; the setup is armed once the counter reaches a threshold.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSinceEmaTouch = (low[0] <= ema(emaLength) && ema(emaLength) <= high[0]) ? 0 : barsSinceEmaTouch[1] + 1; barsSinceEmaTouch >= gapBarThreshold
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context/state precondition, not itself an order)

complexity.reason: EMA plus a persistent streak counter of consecutive non-touch bars

notes: Brooks says 20 is arbitrary ('you can arbitrarily pick any large number of bars'); kept as the book's own default.
Brooks's '2HM' (two hours from the moving average) is a time-based alias for the same concept on a 5 minute chart, not a separate rule.

candidates.name: MovingAverageGapBarPrimitive
candidates.quote: there will likely be a test that goes through the moving average and forms a moving average gap bar where the bar is completely on the other side of the moving average so that there is a gap between the bar and the moving average.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: in a bull trend, the bar's entire range sits below the EMA (no overlap) -- the bar has crossed fully through and past the moving average.

complexity.reason: a single EMA value compared against the bar's high; no window loop or persistent state

notes: Redefined more generally (without the 20-gap-bar precondition) in chapter 14's R14-01.

candidates.name: FirstGapBarFadeEntry
candidates.quote: Look to fade the first gap bar (in a bull trend, buy one tick above the high of the previous bar if the high is below the exponential moving average).
candidates.description: After a 20-gap-bar setup, the first moving-average gap bar triggers a with-trend fade: buy one tick above its high, betting the trend resumes toward its prior extreme.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the high of the gap bar

complexity.reason: composes a moderate streak-counter primitive with a simple EMA test; no new loop needed

notes: Swing part of the position per the book's advice; sizing itself is rejected below as discretion.

candidates.name: SecondGapBarFadeEntry
candidates.quote: If the first entry fails, buy again on the second entry, if there is one.
candidates.description: If the first gap-bar fade entry fails (stops out without the market testing the trend's prior extreme), take the next moving-average gap bar occurrence the same way, as a second attempt.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the high of the second gap bar

complexity.reason: needs a persistent attempt counter that increments on each failed fade and resets once the trend's extreme is tested or a new trend forms

notes: Same 'count to two, then stop' structure as the high/low 1-4 bar counting formalized in chapter 17.

candidates.name: NoThirdGapBarFadeFilter
candidates.quote: it is not worth buying a third time if the first two setups fail since the market at that point is likely in a channel and not forming a reversal.
candidates.description: Block a third consecutive gap-bar fade attempt after two have already failed; treat the market as forming a channel rather than a with-trend bounce.

complexity.reason: reads the same persistent attempt counter as R13-04

candidates.name: ClimaxBeforeSetupInvalidatesGap
candidates.quote: If the market has not touched the moving average for 20 or more bars but there was first a climax, the 20 gap bar setup may not lead to a bounce and a test of the extreme.
candidates.description: Suppress the 20-gap-bar fade if a climax occurred at or before the start of the 20-bar no-touch stretch; expect at least a two-legged correction instead of a simple bounce.

complexity.reason: 'climax' needs a design decision (large-range/exhaustion-bar detection, defined in the Trends volume), and the expected two-legged-correction consequence needs leg counting

notes: Climax primitive is defined in Trends chapter 2 (trend bars, doji bars, and climaxes); this file does not redefine it.

candidates.name: GapBarAfterTrendReversalFailFilter
candidates.quote: if the first moving average gap bar forms after a strong trend reversal, it will likely fail because the trend has now reversed and that gap bar is a setup for the prior trend, which now has ended.
candidates.description: Suppress the moving-average gap-bar fade if a strong trend-direction reversal has just occurred; the gap bar belongs to the prior, now-ended trend.

complexity.reason: depends on a trend-direction-flip primitive (the AlwaysInDirection family) that is itself a design decision

rejected.quote: Moving average tests are particularly reliable in stocks, and often provide great entries all day long.
rejected.reason: asset-class generalization ('stocks' vs. futures/other instruments), not a bar-level condition the engine can test

rejected.quote: since you are trading with the trend, you should swing part of your position because the market may run much further than you thought possible.
rejected.reason: position-sizing/discretion about how much of a position to hold, not a bar-level entry/exit condition

rejected.quote: You can arbitrarily pick any large number of bars and generate a setup that will usually be the same, and it will also work on other time frames.
rejected.reason: meta-commentary about the parameter's arbitrariness and timeframe generality, not itself a testable condition

chapter_summary: Defines the '20 gap bar' setup: once price has run 20+ consecutive bars without touching the 20-bar EMA, the trend is strong but overdone, and the first (then second) bar that gaps fully through the EMA is a with-trend fade back toward the trend's extreme. Produces one moderate EMA/streak-counter primitive (R13-01), a simple gap-bar classification (R13-02, reused verbatim in chapter 14), the first/second fade entries with a hard 'no third attempt' cap (R13-03/04/05, the same counting structure chapter 17 formalizes for H1-4/L1-4), and two research-grade context filters (climax-before-setup, gap-after-reversal) that depend on climax and trend-direction primitives defined elsewhere in the trilogy.
